rationale.paradigm_idiomaticity: The class extends the abstract SpatialLogic and overrides the four required methods, with private static helpers (extractVertices, convexHull, cross, containsInclusive, segmentsIntersect). The contract's public-field data classes limit the object model, but the author added no domain types of their own. Geometry such as a hull, segment or configuration-space builder could have been modelled as small classes, and the helpers are static functions on a stateless class, so the code reads closer to procedural than to OO. That keeps it at 3.
rationale.language_idiomaticity: The code uses List/ArrayList, Comparator.comparingDouble(...).thenComparingDouble(...), diamond operators, a private static final EPS, @Override and a final class. The weaker spots are the raw Point[] 2n buffer with Arrays.asList(...).subList in convexHull, which is a C-style monotone-chain port, and null/empty returns from the status-less contract. The index loops that copy hull points into result.vertices could be a stream or toArray. It is solid but not polished.
rationale.readability: Names are clear (extractVertices, containsInclusive, segmentsIntersect, orient, onSegment). Methods are short enough, except checkDynamicCollision, which mixes csp building, containment and the size 1/2/n cases. There are no comments explaining the Minkowski difference or the epsilon choices. cross and orient are identical, which confuses a reader. A few one-line ifs omit braces.
rationale.design: Responsibilities split into sensible helpers, and the hull is reused by both the sum and the collision check. Extracting vertices defensively into copies is good. Flaws: cross and orient duplicate each other, the sum/difference point-cloud code is duplicated, and the O(nm log nm) all-pairs product followed by a hull is simple but not an edge-merge. The collision check special-cases degenerate hulls inline, and the hull logic is not in a reusable class.

anti_patterns: static utility helpers instead of domain objects (no hull/segment types)
duplicate geometry primitives (cross and orient are identical)
C-style raw Point[] buffer with manual index juggling in convexHull
duplicated cartesian point-cloud loops for sum and difference
justification: The solution correctly extends SpatialLogic and uses Java collections and comparators reasonably, with clearly named private helpers. However, it is essentially procedural: a stateless class of static geometry functions, no added domain types, and duplicated primitives (cross vs orient, duplicated all-pairs loops). The monotone-chain hull uses a C-style array buffer, and checkDynamicCollision is a bit long with inline degenerate-case handling.
